# bob capture-rewrite

Apply the capture grammar's automatic draft rewrites

```text title="bob capture-rewrite --help"
Apply the capture grammar's editor typing assists to TEXT and report the resulting edits, cursor, and a human summary.

The command is purely lexical and completely read-only: it never opens the vault, never reads the clipboard, never touches the filesystem, and takes no --bob-dir. It implements five rules.

Block-ID separator toggle (requires --cursor): typing '^' immediately after a complete plain '@route:id' or '@route+id', ':' after '@route^id' or '@route+id', or '+' after '@route:id' or '@route^id' consumes that character and switches the separator. Typing ':' right after a sealed '@route^id@' gives '@route:id@', and '^' after '@route:id@' gives '@route^id@'. A glued '.' after '@route:id' / '@route^id' switches between ':' and '^' ('@route:id.' becomes '@route^id', and '@route^id.' becomes '@route:id'); after '@route+id' it stays literal. Sealed '@route:id@.' and '@route^id@.' also switch between the two sealed forms. A glued '.' also switches complete task-bullet IDs between ':id' and '^id'. For example, '@file:id+' becomes '@file+id', '@file^id+' becomes '@file+id', '@file+id^' becomes '@file^id', '@file+id:' becomes '@file:id', '@file^id@:' becomes '@file:id@', and '@file:id@^' becomes '@file^id@' (`switch_block_id_separator`). The caret stays just past the unchanged ID (and seal, when sealed). Task IDs at the end of task-list bullets and project-note task bullets also switch: ':id^' becomes '^id', '^id:' becomes ':id', and a glued '.' switches between the two, including nested lines. Only the token ending at --cursor is examined; the key must sit against the ID (or seal) with no space, and it must end the token. Suffixes already inside the token ('#name', '=...'), '@@', '@!', standalone '^route:id', '&note:id', '!note:id', incomplete markers, same-separator repeats after a seal, '+' after a seal, and tokens the contextual parser does not select are left unchanged. On a `>` transfer line, '+' after '@route:id' or '@route^id' in a source or destination slot switches to '@route+id' ('@inbox:bench+ > @db' becomes '@inbox+bench > @db', '@a+x > @c:tid+' becomes '@a+x > @c+tid'); ':' or '^' after a transfer '+id' stays literal, since it would break the transfer. Without --cursor this rule is skipped rather than searching the draft.

Relation-label pipe attach (requires --cursor): typing '|' after whitespace that follows a relation token deletes that whitespace, so '~note:id |' becomes '~note:id|'. Only the '|' token ending at --cursor is examined; it fires only where bob's completion grammar would open a 'relation_label' field, so prose pipes, mid-line relations, already-labelled tokens, partial targets, escapes, and newlines are left unchanged. The caret lands just past the glued '|'. This is an editor assist: 'bob capture' and 'bob capture-parse' keep the literal ' |' text. Without --cursor this rule is skipped rather than searching the draft.

Sigil alias (requires --cursor): typing '.' immediately after '@route' becomes '^', or ';' becomes ':', only where bob's completion grammar would open the corresponding Block ID picker. A '.' glued to a complete '@route:id' / '@route^id' toggles its separator instead of expanding as an alias. A whole-item ';' becomes ':' only where the Task Link picker opens. A '- .' or '- ;' first-level bullet in a sealed project-note item becomes '- ^' or '- :' where the Move picker would open, and '- ^.' becomes '- ^^'. Typing '.' after a space or tab that follows body text becomes '@' wherever a bare '@' would open route completion. It stays literal at a line or bullet-body start, after a checkbox, glued to a word, inside an unclosed backtick span or a wikilink, and in positions with no route field. For example, 'Buy milk .' becomes 'Buy milk @', while '@errands.' still becomes '@errands^' as the first '.' rule. A spaced '.' that does not become '@' becomes '&' wherever a bare '&' would open the Depends On picker, and a spaced ';' that does not become ':' becomes '*' wherever a bare '*' would open the Blocks picker; both follow the same literal positions. For example, '@home .' becomes '@home &' and 'Buy milk ;' becomes 'Buy milk *'. Typing '\' or '/' becomes '#' wherever bob's completion grammar would open a '#' menu: task type, section, drawer and drawer bullet, Pomodoro name, named-start and past-session name, split type, merge destination, and wikilink heading. A '\' or '/' at a line start, glued to a word, or right after another '\' or '/' stays literal. A '/' also stays literal where bob already reads it as part of a field (Go To, the '=/' split, wikilink note paths, section and Pomodoro names); block-ID fields do not count. A '/' glued to a complete '@@route' collapses instead (see the global collapse below). For example, '@cash,' becomes '@cash+', '@cash+goog-exit,' becomes '@cash+goog-exit +', and 'Buy milk ,' becomes 'Buy milk +'; '@errands.' and '@errands;' still become '@errands^' and '@errands:'. Bob's completion grammar decides when a comma is eligible; prose and other picker contexts keep it literal. The aliases use the same picker behavior as the real sigils. Typing '=' after a space or tab aliases '~' only where a bare '~' would open the Links To relation picker. It stays literal at a line or bullet-body start, glued to a word, inside an unclosed backtick span, or inside a wikilink; 'Fix it =' becomes 'Fix it ~', while 'Fix it -' stays literal. Typing '=' after a bare '~' flips it to '~~' (Linked From), and '~~=' flips it back to '~' only where the result opens an empty Links To target. The past-session dash alias still works inside x= tokens, such as 'x=2-' to 'x=2~'. Typing a lowercase 'x' or 's' that ends a close selection aliases '!' (complete) or '*' (park): 'xx' becomes 'x!', 'xs' becomes 'x*', 'x=1=s' becomes 'x=1=*', and '@r:id=xx' becomes '@r:id=x!'. Competing wildcards ('x!s' to 'x!*') stay a viable prefix. The letters stay literal in past names ('x=1s'), after a dangling ',' or '@', on child bullets, and in prose. 'bob capture' and 'bob capture-parse' keep the literal text. Without --cursor this rule is skipped rather than searching the draft.

Global destination collapse (requires --cursor): typing '#', '/', '\', '^', '.', '+', or ',' glued to a complete '@@route' collapses it to '@route#', '@route^', or '@route+' respectively ('/' and '\' become '#', '.' becomes '^', ',' becomes '+'). The route must satisfy the route grammar, the trigger must sit at --cursor with a complete token boundary after it, and the collapsed form keeps the draft's other bytes. Bare '@@', spaced triggers, invalid routes, already-suffixed globals, escaped or quoted prose and code, and triggers earlier than the caret stay literal. The rule is 'collapse_global_destination', carries no alias object or tip, and runs ahead of the sigil aliases above. 'bob capture' and 'bob capture-parse' keep the literal text. Without --cursor this rule is skipped rather than searching the draft.

Relation direction toggle (requires --cursor): typing '~' or '=' immediately after a complete '~note:id' or '~~note:id' flips the direction and consumes the trigger. After a labelled relation, only '~' flips, because '=' is valid label text. The token must be glued to the trigger, be complete, and open a relation target or label in bob's completion grammar; spaced keys, protected or escaped tokens, partial or invalid relations, and text glued after the caret stay unchanged. The cursor lands just past the flipped relation, and the rule is 'toggle_relation_direction'. Without --cursor this rule is skipped rather than searching the draft.

Bare '@@' absorption: typing a bare '@@' inside an item that already carries a local destination marker (or, absent that, when the draft already carries exactly one other '@@' declaration) rewrites the bare token to '@@<payload>', deletes the token it absorbed, and deletes every other declaration token in the draft, so the result always carries at most one declaration. Only the bare '@@' at --cursor (or, when --cursor is omitted, the last bare '@@' in source order) is a candidate. An item whose single local marker cannot be expressed as a declaration -- '@route#Section', '@route+block-id' (an existing task destination), '@route+block-id#section', '@route+block-id!' (a task toggle), '@route^block-id', '@route:block-id', or a trailing bare '#' -- is left untouched with a notice explaining why; an item with more than one local marker is left untouched with no notice, since 'bob capture-parse' already reports that duplicate. Feeding a rewrite's own output back in is a no-op, because the claiming token is no longer bare and no longer ends in a toggle trigger. A whole-item `x[<N>][!<M>]` close item is never rewritten or absorbed, and a `@@` declaration never applies to it. A `>` transfer line never absorbs either: a bare `@@` on the line is left untouched with an `@@ cannot take a capture transfer` notice naming the destination.

Typing tips (requires --cursor): when nothing changed, the JSON 'sigil_alias_tip' field says whether an unshifted alias key would have typed the sigil that ends at --cursor. bob proves it by swapping each candidate key ('.' for '@' '^' '&', ';' for ':' '*', ',' for '+', '=' for '~', '/' or '\' for '#') in for the sigil and running the whole rewrite; a key counts only when that forward rewrite yields exactly TEXT with the caret unchanged. The object carries the lesson 'id', the 'sigil', the preferred 'keys', the sigil's UTF-8 byte 'range', and an optional 'where' phrase. An explicit null means no tip is proved and marks a bob that reports tips; the field is absent without --cursor or when the draft changed. Every rewrite that fires the sigil alias rule also carries an 'alias' object with its 'id', 'key', and 'sigil'. Human output keeps 'no rewrite' and adds one dim 'tip' line.

These assists are editor-only: 'bob capture' and 'bob capture-parse' keep the literal TEXT, so '@file:id^' is not silently rewritten there. Only a missing TEXT or a bad flag is an error; every other input succeeds with 'changed: false' when nothing needed to change. If TEXT is omitted and stdin is piped, it reads the complete piped stdin stream.

Usage: bob capture-rewrite [OPTIONS] [TEXT]...

Arguments:
  [TEXT]...
          Capture text; multiple args are joined with spaces; an unknown `--flag` where TEXT would begin is rejected, later tokens stay literal

Options:
  -c, --cursor <N>
          UTF-8 byte offset of the editor's insertion point

  -f, --format <FORMAT>
          Output format: human or json

          [default: human]
          [possible values: human, json]

  -h, --help
          Show help

Examples:
  bob capture-rewrite -c 17 -f json -- 'Do work @file:id^'
  bob capture-rewrite -c 17 -f json -- 'Do work @file:id.'
  bob capture-rewrite -c 17 -f json -- 'Do work @file:id+'
  bob capture-rewrite -c 17 -f json -- 'Do work @file^id+'
  bob capture-rewrite -c 20 -f json -- 'Fix trip ~work:foo |'
  bob capture-rewrite -c 9 -f json -- '@errands.'
  bob capture-rewrite -c 8 -f json -- 'Fix it ='
  bob capture-rewrite -c 9 -f json -- 'Fix it ~='
  bob capture-rewrite -c 21 -f json -- 'Fix it ~tasks:target='
  bob capture-rewrite -c 6 -f json -- '@cash,'
  bob capture-rewrite -c 16 -f json -- '@cash+goog-exit,'
  bob capture-rewrite -c 1 -f json -- ';'
  bob capture-rewrite -c 10 -f json -- 'Buy milk \'
  printf '@cash^goog-exit@\n- .' | bob capture-rewrite -c 20 -f json
  bob capture-rewrite -c 10 -f json -- 'Buy milk /'
  bob capture-rewrite -c 10 -f json -- 'Buy milk @'
  bob capture-rewrite -c 16 -f json -- 'Buy milk @dev @@'
  bob capture-rewrite -- 'Called Morgan Stanley @cash+goog-exit @@'
  bob capture-rewrite -c 13 -f json -- '@inbox:bench+ > @db'
  bob capture-rewrite -f json -- '@a+x > @c @@'
  printf 'Buy milk @dev @@' | bob capture-rewrite -f json
  printf '@@foo\nBuy milk @@\n' | bob capture-rewrite -f json
  printf 'Buy milk @dev\n- more detail @@\n' | bob capture-rewrite -f json
```
